title: Indiana exchange with Chicago; Pettis goes east
summary: Ashcraft notes Wolverines swapping ideas with the Rhythm Kings, Don Murray replacing Pettis, and Pettis working boats and Ben Bernie in New York.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. The Wolverines were always waiting for Hoagie to come out with another crazy one, or the Marahue brothers down in Indiana. There were others around, you know, at that time. Bob Gillette, who played banjo with the Wolverines, played often with the Rhythm Kings. And Don Murray. And I think Don made angry with them. I think Don was with them a lot, as a matter of fact, on tenor, after Jack Pettis. When we were talking about taking up music as a profession on the part of the Austin boys, everybody knew that the greener fields were in New York. You see, and that was the idea. You were developed in Chicago, and then you go east to the greener fields. Well, the first to go was Pettis. And there were stuff there with stuff there
and so he was replaced with Don Murray in the band because of that
